key_insight: At small fine-tuning budgets, EMA anchored to pretrained weights can confound formula-pretraining comparisons, making last-weight evaluation essential.
engineering_relevance: For label-scarce microstructure-property prediction, audit weight averaging and image contrast conventions before choosing a pretraining strategy.
method: Pretrain ConvNeXt-Small on 150,000 synthetic images using formula regression or masked reconstruction.
Fine-tune conductivity and short-fiber stiffness models with 100, 400, or 1,600 labels.
Recheck results without EMA and test matched versus mismatched phase contrast.
evidence_signal: Without EMA, conductivity formula pretraining had 1.4× ImageNet error across three subsets and five seeds, while stiffness formula pretraining reduced 100-label error by 18% over five seeds.
watch_item: Post hoc contrast-polarity rechecks remained inconclusive across three pretraining runs per polarity, so they do not establish a robust benefit from correcting contrast.
paper_title: Weight Averaging at Small Budgets Confounds Formula-Labeled Pretraining in Microstructure-Property Regression: A Pre-Specified Study with Post Hoc Rechecks
